en: Someone from Dyna Chair coulda leaked it.
No, that's not possible. Park-san had it kept in her safe.
None of the employees even knew she had it.
Then, how?

The answer to that lies in this photo. This was taken twenty
years ago.

It shows Park-san, who was working in showbiz in Tokyo,
along with her husband Majima-san.

Alongside them is Katsuya, who was acting in action movies
at the time.
I spoke with a man who was Katsuya's manager at the time.
Apparently Park-san, Katsuya, and Majima-san...
Have been close friends for the past twenty years.

It sounds like Majima-san helped Katsuya out after he'd
retired from acting.
You said all three of 'em planned it. You don't mean...

I do. It was Katsuya and Park-san themselves that leaked
the info about Majima-san's letter.
I imagine Majima-san and Katsuya were on to Kurosawa's plan.
So they set a trap.
A trap?

They leaked word that Majima-san might still be alive, even
after he was supposedly killed.
They wanted to know who'd take the bait.
The letter was a trap to sniff out who was behind it all.
And they bought it hook, line, and sinker.
So who was it?
Kanai, the Ousaka Enterprises captain working under Katsuya.

Along with Kurosawa, who posed as a detective to get me all
riled up and keep Haruka-chan from leaving Osaka.
Kurosawa was the one after Majima-san's letter.
Ain't Kanai the one who shot Daigo?

Katsuya learned that his man Kanai was actually in league
with Kurosawa.
So he ended up chasing down the letter as well.
He had to hide his connection to Majima-san and the letter itself.
But it was him who rescued Haruka-chan from Kanai.
He also took steps to keep her out of harm's way.

No doubt he was trying to make up for not being able to
protect Park-san.

So Park was a victim who got caught up in Katsuya and
Majima's plan?
I'm pretty sure Park-san realized her situation.

She must have known she was in danger when she got the
letter.

So she gave Haruka-chan her fountain pen, the key to her
safe, to point us in the right direction.

I'm sure she knew that Haruka-chan would carry on her work
if anything ever happened to her.
She must have.

But why would Park cooperate with Majima and Katsuya if she
knew what this was all about?

She's involved with neither the Tojo Clan nor the Omi
Alliance.
I get the feeling she did it for Majima-san.
I doubt she ever intended to see him again.

They lived in different worlds. Even if they loved each
other, it's not like they were destined to cross paths.
She wanted to feel connected to him.

So she kept tabs on Majima-san through Katsuya, and with
her memories of twenty years ago...
She chose the life of a lonely businesswoman.
This place is what connects us with Kiryu-san.

The connection between Park-san and Majima-san, two lovers
destined to live apart⑬
That was Katsuya.
I'm impressed you got all that from a single photo.
You looked into Fukuoka and Nagoya, too, huh?

Ah, no. Actually, I ran into someone who knew all about what
had happened there...
Not that he found out by choice.
And who's that?

A former pro baseball player who came by my office. He's out
seeing a friend right now.
A friend?
Is he okay? He looks like he's in pain.

This here's nothin'. Kiryu's the one who's really in
trouble. We're lucky we even made it here.
Don't you think you should go to the hospital?

Wish I could, but the police'd likely take me in if I went
anywhere near a hospital right now.

Then I'm stuck sittin' on my ass for at least two or three
days, whether I like it or not.
Gotta avoid that at all costs.
Sorry to put this on you.
Oh, it's no trouble for me.
How's he doing?
Not good, huh?
How's Daigo?
It's not pretty. They've got him on life support.
Could be dicey for the next couple of days.

That was a shock, though. The suspect in my murder case
shows up completely out of the blue.
And at Touto University Hospital with Daigo Dojima, no less.

My first thought was that the Tojo Clan and Omi Alliance had
gone to war with one another.
And here I find you guys are involved, too.
Won't ya catch heat, shelterin' us like this?

Are you kidding me? My badge'd be snatched away in a
heartbeat. Again.

But if it gets out, so be it. My detective career basically
started when I first arrested Kiryu, seventeen years ago.
He was there when I quit, and he was there when I came back.

I guess you could say if it wasn't for him, I wouldn't be a
detective in the first place.
Kinda like partners, even if you are on opposite sides of the law.

We're not exactly friends or comrades, but we always end up
thrown together somehow.
We just can't get away from each other, it seems.

Same goes for this place. Seventeen years ago, Kiryu walked
out and took the fall for a friend.
Then, when he found himself back here ten years later...
He got caught up in that ten billion yen incident.

In the seven years since then, he's continued to fight as a
key player in Tokyo's underworld.

Serena seems to be ground zero for all of it, and it brings
in plenty of new faces, too.
I guess you're right.

You could say this place is a crossroads in the life of
Kazuma Kiryu.
There ya are.
I just needed to get some air.
Ya got doubts, huh?
Yeah. I've made up my mind, but it still scares me.

Ever since Kurosawa brought up Haruka, I haven't been able
to get what he said out of my head.
Guy really knows how to get a rise out of people.
I know how ya feel.
It's not just that.

It's been a year since I left Haruka and the kids. Honestly,
it's been... lonely.

Even with new friends and a girl at my side, I still felt
alone.

It's strange. Even when I was locked up, I never felt this
way.
Guess I'm getting old.
Nah. It's about family.
Family?

Seventeen years ago, you had a family. Nishikiyama, Yumi,
your old man Kazama...

So doin' ten years was a breeze, even with them all so far
away.

You had a home to go back to, a family that was always gonna
be there for ya. That's all a guy really needs to stay sane inside.
It was the same for me.

I spent 25 years in that hellhole, but not once did
I lose hope.

I knew Yasuko and my brother Majima would be waitin' for me
when I got out.
Yasuko's gone now, and Majima's who knows where.
But I ain't lonely one bit. Know why?
They chose their paths.

They never took life for granted. They lived and died
entirely on their own terms.

All I can do is fight on and make 'em proud. That's how I
see it, anyway.
Living on your own terms, huh?
Haruka's concert is your call.

If ya wanna give her a shot at her dream, we'll help out in
any way we can.

Ain't no shame in askin' friends for help every now and
then. You got that, Kiryu?
Well, shall we get over to the Japan Dome?
We've got a problem!
The TV. Turn on the TV!

Breaking news: just after 5:00 PM today, the Tokyo
Metropolitan Police issued this announcement.

The Millennium Tower in Kamurocho has
been seized by an unidentified group.

They have taken a hostage⑬Goro Majima, a high-ranking
member of a criminal organization known as the Tojo Clan.
He is being held on the top floor. I repeat, at just after 5:00 PM today...
What the... Majima?
What's our move? The concert is starting soon.
Let's get to Millennium Tower.
There's still time before tomorrow evening.
Tomorrow evening, huh? Looks like I have some time to kill.
We're meetin' up tomorrow evening. Got some time on my hands now.
Tomorrow evening's still a while off. Guess I can do some other stuff.
Rest until noon tomorrow?
There's still time before this evening.
This evening, huh? Looks like I have some time to kill.
We're meetin' up this evening. Got some time on my hands now.
This evening's still a while off. Guess I can do some other stuff.
Rest until this evening?
Okay, how about we each do our own thing until it's time?
Yeah, I'm guessing we all have other things to take care of.
That works.
Sounds good.
Mama said we're welcome to make ourselves at home here.

There's blankets, so feel free to doze off if you need to
rest up.
I think that covers it. Let's meet back here once we're all set to go. Sound good?
Oh yeah, we might as well share what we've got on us, right?
We're all in this together, and I imagine at least one of us is strapped for cash.
You're the one who's probably carryin' the most. So I don't mind if you don't.
Yeah, suits me.
No complaints here!

<Color:7><Color:Default>Each character's funds have been pooled.
A shared Item Box has also been added.

When you access the Item Box, you can now
use items from other characters.

You can change characters now.
Select a character from the hideout menu.
We'll get started tomorrow evening, then!

You're free to explore from now until tomorrow evening.

Use the blankets at New Serena to move time forward.
Once you've done all you want, talk to Kiryu if you are
controlling Akiyama, or otherwise talk to Akiyama.

You can travel to the cities each character is
linked to by taxi.

You can also change characters in each city.
Upon changing characters, you will resume play
in Kamurocho.

It's still an hour before we go on stage. Don't get nervous
just yet.
No... That's not it.
What, then?
Oh, is it boyfriend trouble? Why don't you go call him? You have time.
I hope you can forgive me, Uncle Kaz.
I would've never guessed Aizawa was your son.
When I first joined the yakuza, it was nothing but setback after setback for me.
The first family I joined was some minor, fourth-tier group.
But I finally started climbing the ranks by doing the dirty work no one else wanted to do.
Any of you ever taken the fall for a botched job by <Italic>literally</Italic> eating shit?
People who make it to the top with their pride intact... they were only able to do that because they had a ton of support from many others. I would have loved to keep my pride and integrity...
But nobody had my back.

To get where I am, I had to murder my own aniki.
I had to kill my boss.
...Yes. I got here by wading neck-deep through blood and sweat.
And after sacrificing everything to claw my way up...
The only thing I had, in the end, was power. Nothing else.
Then, six months ago... I thought I just had a touch of pneumonia, but it turned out to be lung cancer.
For the first time in my life, I panicked.

I realized I had nobody to leave my power to. No legacy.
What was the point of it all?
What's goin' on!?
When I give the signal, that girl gets shot.
You should be able to work out the rest, right?
Bastard!
If you want to save Haruka Sawamura, kill your sworn brother.

If Majima wins, I give the signal to shoot.
You can both head on up to heaven together.
But if you win, Saejima, I'll let the girl live.
Then you get to spend the rest of your life behind bars, for taking Majima hostage...
And killing him in retaliation for throwing you out of the Tojo Clan.
What, I thought you'd enjoy rotting in a cell.
You twisted fuck.
Bro... We really doin' this?
We don't, and her dream dies in front of 50,000 people.

You and I kick the bucket, though⑬nobody'd bat an eye.
The choice ain't hard.
How ya gonna fight me all banged up like that?

Ya won't last five minutes. We ain't even on the same
playing field.

Ya said so yourself. You ain't what ya used to be.
You don't have it in ya to take me on.
You're right about that.
Then what're ya doin'!?
Two years ago, I couldn't fight you.
That's because... ya were too damn weak!
Huh? The hell?
It's true. I saw all I needed to at that battin' center.
Gettin' out of the slammer, comin' back to the Tojo... it softened ya up.
But I knew what I had to do. 'Cause in our world, it's all over when ya go soft. That's why I gave ya an easy out.
The expulsion letter. It wasn't Morinaga or Aoyama who wrote it.
It was me. I sent it as I was headin' out to Sapporo!
...How could ya?
Bro, I really didn't want ya dragged back into this.
I didn't think that legend about you killin' eighteen men... would make ya such a target.
Now get that shirt off. Time to prove ya still got what it takes!
I wanna see those fangs shinin' bright as they did in the old days.
The Tojo patriarchs...
Excuse me, is the president here?
That'd be me. And you are?
Suzuki, from Nagasu Taxi.
I broke the rules today when I picked up a passenger midway through the line, so I'm here to apologize.
Oh, so that was you?
Guess y'take after your boss Nakajima. No sense among the lot of ya.
